rationale: shared.syntax defines p, x and f; shared.state defines S, q, alpha and kappa and slot lookup. This unit then introduces the mode-annotated resolution judgment and its variable/field cases before path-exclusivity uses it. Resolve.variable reads a present initialized variable and returns that reference's mode. Resolve.field requires an already resolved prefix, the containing object, and an initialized named field, then returns permission.join reference.mode. Mode.join is unique only for the unique/unique pair and shared in every other case, exactly as in the displayed table. Resolve is indexed by one unchanged state and performs no update. Empty or absent route slots and absent intermediate objects satisfy neither constructor. The prose appropriately specifies intermediate objects: resolution itself does not require the final target to be allocated in an arbitrary malformed raw State; later well-formedness supplies target allocation.
